harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log with seven compressed rotations and copytruncate. Live-write behavior, system integration, reboot persistence, and post-reboot recovery were all verified on node1.
actions_performed: Created /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with daily, rotate 7, compress, missingok, notifempty, and copytruncate.
Validated the rule through the host's global logrotate configuration and successfully ran logrotate.service.
Forced a live rotation while a writer held the log open; the inode remained unchanged and writing continued.
Safely rebooted node1, observed a changed boot identity, and verified configuration, scheduler, archives, and data recovery.
Repeated the live rotation test after reboot and removed the temporary boot-ID evidence file.

evidence.requirement: Rotate app.log daily and keep seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: The installed and globally parsed policy reports daily rotation with rotate count 7; an actual valid gzip rotation was created and logrotate.service completed successfully.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Before and after reboot, a held-open writer wrote successfully after forced rotation while app.log retained inode 9912367; pre-rotation data appeared in gzip archives and post-rotation data appeared in the active log.

The healthy baseline used boot ID d4784d1b-162e-4faa-b581-f6427617d23c; the safe delayed systemctl reboot was acknowledged; recovery showed boot ID 69ec46f7-2011-4a84-a810-f02e189bc1e1, running system state, enabled/active timer, persisted policy, valid archives, preserved original data, and successful post-reboot rotation/service execution.
Final boot ID remained the new identity; logrotate.timer was enabled and active, the configuration and active log were present, and two compressed rotations existed from verification.
